bank.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
bank.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

outcomes.description: Transform the image into a pencil drawing.
outcomes.target: The image is rendered as a pencil drawing, with its visual content represented in a pencil-drawn style.
outcomes.reference: The supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation.

bank.reason: One fact can assess whether pencil-drawing treatment is present at all; a second can distinguish a completed image-wide rendering from localized or incomplete treatment. No source-content preservation condition is needed.

facts.question: Is pencil-drawing treatment visibly present anywhere in the edited image?
facts.present_when: Visible pencil-like drawn strokes, hatching, or shading appear in at least some part of the image.
facts.absent_when: The image is clearly assessable and shows no visible pencil-drawing treatment.
facts.unknown_when: The image is too unclear to determine whether any pencil-drawing treatment is present.

facts.question: Is the edited image rendered throughout as a pencil drawing?
facts.present_when: Pencil-drawing treatment is visibly applied throughout the image, rather than being limited to isolated areas, and the image reads as a pencil drawing overall.
facts.absent_when: The image is clearly assessable and is not rendered throughout as a pencil drawing, including when treatment is absent or limited to only part of the image.
facts.unknown_when: The image is too unclear to determine whether pencil-drawing treatment covers the image overall.

decisions.partial_when: F1 is present and F2 is absent.
decisions.unknown_when: F1 is unknown, or F1 is present and F2 is unknown.

F1.evidence: The edited image has a muted, pencil-like appearance with visible fine drawn texture and shading across the food and surrounding objects.

F2.evidence: The edited image is clearly assessable and retains a photographic appearance with muted colors; it does not read as a pencil drawing throughout.
